messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Fwd: stan runtime error "Exception: boost::too_many_args: format-string referred..."
parts:
Thanks, Ben.

The issue is that one of our distributions is improperly formatting the error message. That throws a different type of exception. My guess is that we don't catch that particular exception in the leapfrog step and it dies.

My guess is that it's happening in either the multi_normal or inv_wishart distributions. I'm pretty sure the univariate tests would catch this error.

I'll try to hunt it down and fix it.



Daniel

Honestly, I'm confused by it too. The documentation is here:
http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_52_0/libs/format/doc/format.html

Since we're still using Boost's exception throwing mechanism (if you follow our error checking back to Boost, you'll find it), we are tied to it. Last I checked, the Boost function uses the default formatter and feeds it one argument. If "%1%" is not specified, we get that error. If we specify "%2%" or any higher number, we also trigger that error. I haven't found a way to drop the argument to the floor -- that's why the error messages in the multivariate distributions show the (0,0) element.

Any *.stan file in that folder will be compiled with the test/gm/compile_models test. To get them to be part of the parser test, we still have to edit the test by hand: src/test/gm/parser_test.cpp.

For right now, we've got the unit tests compiling those Stan models, but we don't actually run them. Should we be checking the exit code? Or something else? I'm not sure what's the best way to detect the proper behavior.
